body: Will this ultimately have an effect on load times?

This takes the place of what was previously a whole new load. I don't think so .

This path happening at all is also extremely rare. I ran the MRP for about 10 minutes and only saw this getting hit a handful of times. 

I think that for the cases where this code runs, it's a performance improvement.

Wouldn't it possible to use WorkerThreadPool::get_singleton()->wait_for_task_completion instead of this loop? I'm not sure but maybe we would just need to store the id of the task actually loading the resource in ThreadLoadTask.

If I'm not mistaken if we reach this code we already called WorkerThreadPool::get_singleton()->wait_for_task_completion on the load_task. Do we really need this loop? The status should always be THREAD_LOAD_LOADED of THREAD_LOAD_FAILED at this point.
That is what the old code did. That is what caused the bugs :)

No, that is the bug that this PR fixes. `wait_for_task_completion()` won't let you wait on an "older" task. The previous behavior was to then restart the task. Which caused the bug. That's why we wait now.

Indeed, I remember now! IMO it's a bit complicated and error-prone to have two ways of wait for task completion, maybe we can change the inner logic of wait_for_task_completion (I don't know if it's something used elsewhere), or add an helper method in ResourceLoader to automatically wait the right way. Anyway it's not my call at all, I'm curious of what @RandomShaper will think of that.

Sorry maybe my comment was not clear enough, I will try to put it another way. 

In this else block we are in the path were `wait_for_task_completion` agreed to wait (it didn't returned `ERR_BUSY`) and `restart` is false, so the resource should already be loaded. 

If not we would have entered the `if (restart)` path and called `_run_load_task` that you modified to wait for the already running older task, which is actually fixing the duplicated load issue.
I think I maybe see what you are saying, I'll look at the logic again

I didn't want to change the behaviour of the workerthreadpool, the logic is used elsewhere in the engine and is exposed to scripting and GDExtension.

I don't think we should change the behaviour in a bug fix. It would have to be a PR to specifically change the thread pool I think.
It looks like this `return` skips cleaning up `own_mq_override`, leaking it.

I looked at it again. You are right, the else branch is unreachable. Or rather, if it can be reached it is pointless to wait as the task has completed by then.

I left that in from a previous fix and didn't realize it was now redundant.

Thanks a lot!
You are correct,  and the current logic doesn't actually need this anymore! Thanks!
